report.summary: Episodic buffers (MemPrompt) improved code synthesis ~10%. Reflection (Reflexion) boosted AlfWorld & HotpotQA by 11–18%, HumanEval by 60% relative. Skill libraries (Voyager) collected 3.3x more items in Minecraft. Structured world models are less mature; MemoryBank improved conversation consistency. For code agents, reflection yields the largest, most replicable gains.
risks: Reflection may reinforce biases if past failures are not pruned or diversified.
Skill libraries risk explosion of niche code snippets with high retrieval overhead.
Episodic buffers can suffer from irrelevant retrieval, degrading output quality.
Structured world models require careful design to avoid brittle schemas.
todos: Evaluate Reflexion-style episodic memory on Daedalus code generation/evolution tasks.
Implement a persistent store of error-correction pairs with semantic retrieval.
Test combining skill library (reusable code snippets) with reflection for iterative improvement.
Monitor retrieval latency and relevance trade-offs.

handoff.suggestion: Integrate a reflection-based episodic memory that stores and retrieves past error-correction pairs. Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) achieved measured gains: on AlfWorld it improved GPT-3.5 ReAct from 78.5% to 89.7%, on HotpotQA from 34.6% to 52.8%, and on HumanEval code synthesis from a CoT baseline of 12.5% to 20.1% (60% relative increase). These gains come from persistent, structured verbal feedback (reflections) that guide similar future tasks. For Daedalus, this means storing failed code attempts, the critic feedback, and the corrected code, then using similarity search to inject relevant experiences into prompts. The overhead is low: only text storage and retrieval, unlike Voyager's heavy skill library or world model maintenance. Start with a simple vector store (e.g., FAISS) over code embeddings (e.g., CodeBERT) to retrieve top-3 similar experiences, appending them as few-shot examples. This is the most actionable step because it directly lifts success rates on code tasks, requires minimal infrastructure, and has strong published evidence across multiple benchmarks.
